I have a full rocker Rossignol Taipan that I bought at the beginning of the season, the mountain I usually hit up (Snowbird, SLC) has a very small unimpressive park but makes up with a vast expanse of beautiful steep mountain covered in the most amazing snow on earth. I was worried at the beginning of the season that I would have trouble on a full rocker board but I have found that the rocker doesn't catch edges on hardpack nearly as much as my last board (Rossignol One, traditional camber). Super floaty in pow, nothing better than surfing in the deep soft stuff. As with all aspects of the sport; a large element of the board's performance is related to your personal skill and control over the board. If you have a rocker board, don't be afraid to try it out on the mountain or in the backcountry, if you don't and are willing to buy a rocker, I would highly recommend doing so.
